ORIGINAL ARTICLE
Constrained optimal power ﬂow and optimal TCSC allocation
using hybrid cuckoo search and ant lion optimizer
Sheila Mahapatra 1 • Nitin Malik 2 • Saurav Raj 3 • Mohan Krishna Srinivasan 1
Received: 13 May 2021 / Revised: 30 June 2021 / Accepted: 27 August 2021 / Published online: 25 September 2021
/C211The Society for Reliability Engineering, Quality and Operations Management (SREQOM), India and The Division of Operation and
Maintenance, Lulea University of Technology, Sweden 2021
Abstract This paper works on the solution to Voltage
Constrained Optimal Power Flow (VCOPF) problem with
the requisite allocation of thyristor-controlled series com-
pensator (TCSC) in IEEE 6-bus and 14-bus transmission
network to cut down system power losses and to revamp
bus voltage proﬁle. The Newton–Raphson algorithm
computes the power ﬂow under normal and overloaded
operating conditions. The optimal TCSC location is iden-
tiﬁed by the Cuckoo Search algorithm (CS) and optimal
size is determined using an ant-lion optimizer (ALO). The
quadratic fuel cost is chosen as the objective and is sub-
jugated to the equality and inequality constraints. The
proposed methodology is validated by contrasting the
results to the other hybrid methods such as Fuzzy-Gravi-
tational search algorithm (F-GSA), Improved GSA-Fireﬂy
algorithm (IGSA-FA) and Radial basis function neural
network-GSA (RBFNN-GSA). The statistical analysis is
also carried out for validating the efﬁcacy of the algorithm
when compared with other reported methods in the litera-
ture. The simulation results obtained on standard test
systems manifest the improved performance of proposed
hybrid cuckoo search and ant lion optimizer (CS-ALO) in
comparison with the other optimization techniques that
have emerged in the recent state-of-the-art-literature.
Keywords TCSC /C1 Optimal allocation /C1 Ant-lion
optimizer /C1 Cuckoo search /C1 Optimal power ﬂow
1 Introduction
1.1 Motivation
The optimal power ﬂow (OPF) integrates the power ﬂow
with the dispatch to minimize the fuel cost subject to
equality and inequality constraints. The non-linearity
Newton method appreciably addresses the marginal losses
but the linear programming is more useful in determining
the boundary limits. While solving the OPF problem, the
system safety parameters such as voltage violations and
thermal capacity of the lines must be regulated precisely
(Charles et al. 2020; Weinhold and Mieth 2020). The OPF
solution helps to identify the maximum transfer capacity of
tie-lines (Abbasi et al. 2021; Reddy 2019; El-Fergany and
Hasanien 2020). The security appraisal helps to ascertain if
the power system in a normal state can survive the con-
tingencies (Zhang et al. 2019). The power system safety
must be taken care of for smooth functioning of complex
interconnected network (Naderi et al. 2019; Taher et al.
2019). The literature survey has revealed that not much
attention has been put up on simultaneously solving the
voltage-constrained OPF problem and optimal allocation of
TCSC. This has motivated the authors to work in this
direction.

1.2 Recent research work
The FACTS devices are positioned to shrink the power
ﬂows in overloaded power lines, thereby providing a pro-
tective mechanism, bringing down power wastage and
boosting the voltage consistency. Thyristor Controlled
Series Compensator (TCSC) is a series-connected FACTS
device that provides precise power control, damps inter-
area oscillations, alleviate subsynchronous resonance and
steps up transient stability.
Jordehi ( 2015) has proposed a brainstorm optimization
algorithm to ﬁnd the optimal position and control setting of
static var compensators (SVC) and TCSC but the problem
of OPF is not addressed. Subhojit Dawn et al . (Dawn and
Tiwari 2016) presented a gradual change in TCSC regu-
lating parameters and uniﬁed power ﬂow controller
(UPFC) for their allocation but the comparison of results
with that obtained from hybrid approach is not carried out.
Jordehi ( 2016) proposed an imperialistic competitive
algorithm for the TCSC allocation problem that resulted in
low voltage deviation and overloads during load growth
and contingencies when compared to gravitational search
algorithm (GSA) and bat swarm optimization but the
generation cost optimization has not been carried out.
K. Pandiarajan and Babulal ( 2016) integrate fuzzy and
harmony search algorithm to curtail the complete cost of
generation fuel and obtained an OPF solution but both
TCSC location and size not optimized. Naresh et al. ( 2016)
employed an improved Harmony Search Algorithm for the
coordinated TCSC design and power system stabilizers to
effectively damp oscillations but TCSC allocation has not
been proposed. The authors in Sekhar and Mohanty ( 2016)
developed an upgraded cuckoo search algorithm for con-
tingency constrained economic power dispatch aiming to
relieve system overloading but FACT devices have not
been incorporated. The authors in Abd-Elazim and Ali
(2016) applied the cuckoo search (CS) algorithm for
parameter tuning of STATCOM in a multi-machine system
but optimization of generation cost has not been carried
out. The authors in Nguyen ( 2016) proposed a CS algo-
rithm for generating a solution to a combined heat and
power load dispatch problem with a prime objective of fuel
cost minimization but TCSC has not been incorporated.
The cuckoo search algorithm (Nartu et al. 2019)i s
employed for reducing transmission losses by optimally
placing FACT device but fuel generation cost not included.
A novel hybrid algorithm (Dash et al. 2020a) exploited the
properties of recent algorithms to minimize the losses and
identify the location of TCSC and SVC in IEEE 14 bus and
30 bus systems but the OPF not considered. The installa-
tion cost was considered as the ﬁtness function. Authors in
Hocine and Djamel ( 2019) applied a genetic algorithm for
sizing and placing UPFC. Several algorithms (Mahapatra
et al. 2019; Dash et al. 2020b; Abed-alguni and Alkhateeb
2020) emphasized cutting down of network power wastage
and improving the node voltage proﬁle simultaneously
under normal and overloading instances. Salp swarm
algorithm (SSA) is applied in Mahapatra et al. ( 2020)t o
determine the optimal reactive power planning in an
interlinked network. The convergence is improved by
coupling the Oppositional-based learning concept with the
oppositional SSA and validated in a standard IEEE 57
benchmark system. Optimal power ﬂow problems have
been addressed in detail in Mahdad ( 2020), Nguyen 2019,
Manusov et al. 2018) where single, as well as multiple
objectives, are incorporated. The elimination mechanism is
chosen over a selection mechanism to simplify selection
efforts. The solutions with fast searchability were proposed
and the objective functions were centred around the fuel
cost, power loss, and voltage proﬁle. In Raj et al. ( 2021),
the authors applied salp swarm algorithm (SSA) and quasi-
oppositional SSA for optimal TCSC placement in IEEE 14-
and 57-bus system. In Failed ( 2021), the author utilized a
modiﬁed branch-and-bound algorithm by application of
depth-ﬁrst search algorithm followed by breadth-ﬁrst
search algorithm in solution to the problem. In (Babu et al.
2020), the authors proposed a new voltage stability indi-
cator in identifying the weakest bus. In Dey et al. ( 2020),
author’s hybrid combination of grey wolf optimizer, sine–
cosine algorithm and crow search algorithm to minimize
the generation cost. In Parihar and Malik ( 2017), the total
system cost for generation is optimized by considering
Economic load dispatch and Environmental Dispatch
simultaneously.
1.3 Paper contribution
Currently, voltage constrained optimal power ﬂow
(VCOPF) problem is one of the most demanding problem
and a crucial aspect to be considered for transmission
expansion planning. It has been observed from the litera-
ture review that attempting simultaneous OPF solution
with voltage consistency management and optimal FACTS
controller allocation is an extremely challenging task. So,
many of the existing algorithms individually may not
produce best results when applied to complex power sys-
tem optimization issues with multiple constraints. So,
hybrid algorithms are most suited to tackle such complex
optimization as they are designed and implemented for
handling numerous large-scale, multimodal real-world
problems. This research work utilizes the best attributes of
CS-ALO hybrid algorithm in addressing the VCOPF
problem. The summarized contribution of this paper is
given as follows:
123
722 Int J Syst Assur Eng Manag (April 2022) 13(2):721–734

(a) Hybrid Cuckoo search (CS)-ant lion optimizer
(ALO) algorithms are solicited to solve optimal
locale and sizing of TCSC respectively.
(b) The independent approaches for the optimal position
and TCSC size provide the versatility of the
approach to the problem. The results can be
independently utilized for further use.
(c) The results obtained are superior in terms of losses
and TCSC cost when compared to the results in the
published work. It also generates improved voltage
proﬁle.
(d) The outcomes signify that the recommended tech-
nique is feasible for implementation in large power
networks with the incorporation of FACT devices.
1.4 Organization
Section 1 deals with the motivation to use a hybrid CS
algorithm—Ant-Lion optimizer (ALO) to solve TCSC
allocation in IEEE standard bus systems, literature review
and the contribution of this paper. Section 2 covers the
mathematical modelling of the OPF problem and TCSC
allocation. Section 3 and 4 discuss the CS and ALO.
Section 5 covers the solution methodology for TCSC
allocation. Section 6 deals with results and discussion on
two standard test systems. The conclusions are drawn
ﬁnally.
2 Problem formulation and modelling of TCSC
OPF problem formulation aims at truncating the fuel cost
which is the main component of generation cost. However,
in the current work the authors also aim to enhance the
system voltage proﬁle of the complex interconnected net-
work. So, the problem formulation in the work proposed is
voltage constrained OPF solution with optimal TCSC
placement.

2.2 TCSC modelling
A TCSC comprises of capacitor shunting anti-parallel
SCRs and an inductor. The delay angle variation regulates
the reactance of the thyristors comprising the TCSC. As the
power delivery capability of a transmission line is inversely
related to net reactance offered by the path inclusion of
TCSC in series with the line diminishes the transfer reac-
tance. This eventually leads to the enhancement of maxi-
mum power transfer of the line coupled with the reduction
in reactive power loss. The modes of operation of TCSC
may be inductive or capacitive and the level of compen-
sation is guided by Eq. ( 12) to ignore over-compensation.

is provided in Fig. 1.

4 Ant lion optimizer
Ant Lion Optimizer (ALO) is a bio-inspired algorithm that
mimics the predator and pasturing ability of antlions
(Mirjalili 2015). The larva stage is dominated by foraging
and is engaged in the reproduction cycle on maturity. The
antlions are characterized by their strange circular move-
ment to establish cone-shaped dugouts in the sand. These
are halting station where they wait to capture their prey
(ants). The pits size has a direct inﬂuence by moon size and
the starvation level of the antlion. The cone-shaped struc-
ture of dugouts is staged in such a manner that it is
Fig. 1 Representation of TCSC inception in power line
123
724 Int J Syst Assur Eng Manag (April 2022) 13(2):721–734

slippery, and ants can easily be trapped into it. The ALO
algorithm is characterized by ﬁve vital steps: arbitrary
movement of ants, building trap pits, deceiving the ants and
reconstruction of the dugouts for the next prey.
The ALO method is an adaptation of this interlinkage
between antlion and the ants as predator and prey. Math-
ematically modelling this bio-inspired interdependency
requires a stochastically driven approach. The ant matrix is
randomly initialized and upgrade in position to the next
level is decided by the roulette wheel operator and the elite.
To avert excessive divergence in search space, the bounds
are speciﬁed corresponding to the current iteration. The
arbitrary movement of ants around selected elite and
antlion is carried out until all the prey are evaluated and
ﬁtness is evaluated.
The advantages associated with the ALO technique are
numerous such as the ability to reach global optima due to
ample diversiﬁcation in search space by arbitrary antlion
selection, ﬂexible contraction of antlions boundaries and
strengthened probability to prevent local optima stagnation
due to diversiﬁed population (Dubey et al. 2016).
5 Solution methodology for optimal TCSC
allocation

combinedly established by using CS and ALO algorithm.
The optimal allocation depends on the indices such as
Apparent Power Flow (API), voltage variance (V D), power
dissipated (P L) and cost of TCSC (C TCSC). The best TCSC

6 Results and discussion

applied to evaluate the best siting and the capacity of the
TCSC controller. The proposed methodology is also uti-
lized to upgrade the voltage consistency at the buses with
TCSC connected system. The work is implemented on

6.2 Test System 2- IEEE 14 bus
The efﬁcacy of the proposed algorithm is also evaluated on
IEEE 14 power network. The power ﬂow computed using
N-R method with the base case loading condition and to
ascertain the efﬁcacy of the CS-ALO algorithm load of the
